claim: About half of Drosophila protein-coding genes still lack functional characterization.
source: Although Drosophila is one of the most intensively studied organisms, about half of Drosophila protein-coding genes still lack functional characterization (Ewen-Campen et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ewen-Campen et al., 2017

claim: Genome-wide loss-of-function screens using RNA interference or CRISPR-Cas9 have helped elucidate the mechanisms of a variety of biological processes in Drosophila.
source: In Drosophila, genome-wide LOF screens using RNA interference or CRISPR-Cas9 have helped elucidate the mechanisms of a variety of biological processes (Boutros et al., 2004; Björklund et al., 2006; D'Ambrosio and Vale, 2010; Bard et al., 2006; Guo et al., 2008; Hao et al., 2008; Song et al., 2022; Viswanatha et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: Genome-wide gain-of-function screens have not been feasible in Drosophila, largely due to a lack of reagents for genome-scale GOF perturbation.
source: However, genome-wide GOF screens have not been feasible, largely due to a lack of the reagents for genome-scale GOF perturbation.
evidence: Statement about the state of the field based on established knowledge

claim: Current state-of-the-art for Drosophila GOF studies utilizes cDNA library overexpression, which only covers a subset of the genome and underrepresents genes with long open reading frames.
source: Current state-of-the-art for Drosophila GOF studies utilizes cDNA library overexpression (Stapleton et al., 2002; Yu et al., 2011), which only covers a subset of the genome and underrepresents genes with long open reading frames (ORFs).
evidence: Supported by citations and established knowledge about cDNA library limitations

claim: Nuclease-dead Cas9 (dCas9) fused with transcriptional activators and targeted to the promoter region by sgRNAs can facilitate transcription at endogenous loci.
source: Nuclease-dead Cas9 (dCas9) is fused with different transcriptional activators and targeted to the promoter region by single-guide RNAs (sgRNAs) to facilitate transcription at endogenous loci.
evidence: Description of established CRISPRa mechanism

claim: Synergistic activation mediator (SAM) complex is one of the most efficient CRISPRa systems.
source: Synergistic activation mediator (SAM) complex is one of the most efficient CRISPRa systems (Konermann et al., 2015; Chavez et al., 2016).

claim: CRISPR-based GOF approaches have been used for genome-wide genetic screens in mammalian cells.
source: CRISPR-based GOF approaches have been used for genome-wide genetic screens in mammalian cells (Konermann et al., 2015; Rodríguez et al., 2022; Zhu et al., 2022; Sofer et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2022), but the feasibility has not yet been tested in Drosophila cells.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: The feasibility of CRISPR-based GOF approaches has not yet been tested in Drosophila cells.
source: CRISPR-based GOF approaches have been used for genome-wide genetic screens in mammalian cells (Konermann et al., 2015; Rodríguez et al., 2022; Zhu et al., 2022; Sofer et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2022), but the feasibility has not yet been tested in Drosophila cells.
evidence: Statement about the state of the field at the time of the study

claim: A pooled genome-wide CRISPRa screening platform was developed in Drosophila cells using the SAM complex.
source: To address this gap, we developed a pooled genome-wide CRISPRa screening platform in Drosophila cells using the SAM complex.

claim: Focused and genome-wide CRISPRa screens identified novel candidates conferring rapamycin resistance.

claim: CG5399 overexpression activates the RTK-Akt-mTOR signaling pathway.

The sgRNAs specifically activated CG9877, but not CG13538 (Figure 1C), suggesting that the SAM complex activates the target gene without affecting nearby genes at least in some divergent gene pairs.
